# Limitations

## Current execution

The supplied StudyChat input is a sample derivative rather than a complete export. Candidate yield, anomaly rates, privacy signals, components, and splits from this execution are pilot observations only. The aggregate full-corpus values in the attached metadata cannot establish complete coverage.

No full natural WikiConv artifact is acquired or processed here. WikiConv reconstruction, lineage, mining, and split behavior are exercised with synthetic fixtures, so natural WikiConv item counts and performance are unavailable.

No independent human annotation, adjudication, manual privacy approval, legal approval, public release decision, or model experiment has occurred. Constructor judgments are provisional and cannot support scientific performance claims.

## Construct validity

Atomic write-time governance is a narrower task than complete memory-system behavior. An item can be valid under the benchmark while omitting broader dialogue objectives, retrieval policy, storage cost, or downstream response quality. Conversely, some real memory decisions are too entangled to fit one atomic slot and are excluded.

The distinction between `KEEP` and `ABSTAIN` can remain difficult in underspecified natural language. Prospective annotation and ambiguity analyses are required to determine whether the ontology is reliable across scopes.

## Domain coverage

StudyChat emphasizes educational programming and related task interaction. WikiConv emphasizes collaborative editorial work. Neither track represents all natural conversation, all personal memory, all workplaces, all languages, or all social contexts. WikiConv is not personal-assistant memory, and StudyChat items are not uniformly long-term personal preferences.

## Source and reconstruction

Repeated cumulative histories can be inconsistent with canonical prompt-response rows. Source exports may omit edits, deleted material, moderation context, or external evidence. Wiki revision actions do not necessarily reveal consensus, and talk-page discussion does not necessarily reveal implementation.

## Privacy

Automated redaction cannot guarantee anonymity. Rare content, artifact names, cross-session linkage, contributor behavior, and deleted text can remain identifying. Strong privacy transformations can also alter the decision. Human review and possible exclusion are mandatory.

## Licensing

Machine-collected license evidence is not legal advice or approval. Dataset wrappers and underlying content can have different terms. Attribution, ShareAlike, modification notice, deleted-content handling, and derivative redistribution remain unresolved until a recorded human decision applies to the exact package.

## Evaluation

Natural prevalence may be highly imbalanced, continuity components may be large, and some scopes may have limited support. Kappa is prevalence-sensitive. Even cluster bootstrap confidence intervals do not correct construct bias, source sampling bias, or annotator-selection bias.

Cross-domain transfer can reflect vocabulary and discourse differences rather than a general memory-governance capability. Trajectory evaluation introduces compounding dependencies and requires real adjudicated sequences before conclusions are possible.

## Temporal validity

Venue rules, dataset access terms, upstream artifacts, model providers, and URLs can change. Snapshots are dated and must be refreshed before submission or release.
